134.body:
# Chapter 1: Laws Related to Driving

There are 4 important laws that drivers need to know, namely: the Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522, the Land Transport Act B.E. 2522, the Highway Act B.E. 2535, and the Road Traffic Act B.E. 2522.

## 1.1 Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522

Vehicles under the control of the Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522 consist of:

- Private passenger cars not exceeding 7 persons (sedans)
- Private passenger cars exceeding 7 persons but not exceeding 12 persons, which are not used for commercial transport for hire under the Land Transport Act
- Private trucks with a weight not exceeding 1,600 kilograms, which are not used for commercial transport for hire under the Land Transport Act
- Inter-provincial hire cars used for carrying passengers not exceeding 7 persons
- Hire cars for carrying passengers not exceeding 7 persons
- Service cars used for carrying passengers for hire or for rent not exceeding 7 persons
- Private motorcycles
- Public motorcycles
- Private three-wheeled vehicles
- Three-wheeled hire vehicles
- Road rollers
- Tractors
- Trailers
- Agricultural vehicles

### 1) Registration, Markings, and Use of Vehicles

1.1 Vehicles brought into use must be registered and have annual taxes fully and correctly paid. Any person who uses a vehicle without registration or tax payment shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 10,000 baht.

1.2 A vehicle eligible for registration must have complete and correct essential components and equipment as prescribed in the ministerial regulations and must have passed a vehicle inspection in accordance with the criteria, methods, and conditions prescribed in the ministerial regulations at the time of registration. Any person who uses a vehicle with incomplete or incorrect essential components or equipment as prescribed in the ministerial regulations, or adds anything that may cause harm to the body or mind of others, shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht.

1.3 To apply for vehicle registration, an application shall be submitted to the registrar of the locality where the applicant is domiciled.

1.4 A registered vehicle must have and display license plates and markings completely and correctly as prescribed in the ministerial regulations. Any person who violates this shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht.

1.5 Any change of vehicle color that differs from the registered color must be reported by the vehicle owner to the registrar within 7 days from the date of the color change. Any person who violates this shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht.

135.body:
1.6 For the transfer of a registered vehicle, both the transferor and the transferee must notify the registrar within 15 days from the date of transfer. Any person who violates this shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht.

1.7 When relocating a vehicle to a different locality, the vehicle owner must notify the local registrar within 15 days from the date of relocation. Any person who violates this shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht.

1.8 A registered vehicle shall not be altered in its body or any part thereof to differ from the registered particulars and then used, unless the owner first brings it to the registrar for inspection. Any person who violates this shall be liable to a fine not exceeding 2,000 baht.

1.9 "Red plates" are special markings issued by the Department of Land Transport to vehicle dealerships for use on vehicles only for the purpose of delivering them to customers or taking them for repairs. They are permitted to be driven only between sunrise and sunset, or during daytime only. The general public may not use red-plate vehicles on public roads at any time. If a vehicle bearing red plates that has not yet been registered and has not had its annual tax properly paid is used on the road, it constitutes an offense under the Motor Vehicle Act B.E. 2522, punishable by a fine not exceeding 10,000 baht.

2) Vehicles Exempt from Registration

2.1 Vehicles of the Royal Thai Police Department that are registered and bear markings as prescribed by the Director-General of the Royal Thai Police Department.

2.2 Vehicles of the Bureau of the Royal Household that are registered and bear markings as prescribed by the Secretary-General of the Royal Household.

2.3 Vehicles for which the owner has declared non-use.

2.4 Vehicles that the manufacturer or assembler has produced for sale, or that the importer has imported for sale, and that have been manufactured, assembled, or imported but have not yet been sold to others.

3) Vehicles Exempt from Fees, Except for License Plate Fees

3.1 Fire engines.

3.2 Ambulances that are not for-hire vehicles.

3.3 Vehicles of ministries, sub-ministries, departments, municipalities, provincial administrative organizations, sanitary districts, Bangkok Metropolitan Administration, Pattaya City, and other local government bodies — limited to vehicles not used for commercial purposes or profit.

3.4 Road rollers of state enterprises.

3.5 Tractors of state enterprises.

3.6 Vehicles of the Thai Red Cross Society.

3.7 Vehicles of persons in diplomatic missions, consular missions, international organizations, or specialized agencies of the United Nations stationed in Thailand.

3.8 Agricultural vehicles as specified by the characteristics and conditions prescribed in ministerial regulations.

4) Classification of Motor Vehicle Types and Seat Belt Designs

4.1 Notification of the Department of Land Transport regarding the specification of characteristics and installation of seat belts for motor vehicles, B.E. 2553, which shall not apply to small four-wheeled vehicles, small four-wheeled for-hire vehicles, three-wheeled private vehicles, and three-wheeled for-hire vehicles. The notification specifies two types of seat belts:

(1) Three-point belt (lap and shoulder belt)

(2) Lap belt

138.body:
(2) Other motor vehicles not specified in (1), while towing a trailer, trucks with a vehicle weight including load weight exceeding 1,200 kilograms, or three-wheeled motor vehicles, shall be driven within the Bangkok Metropolitan Area, Pattaya City Area, or municipal areas at a speed not exceeding 45 kilometers per hour, or outside such areas at a speed not exceeding 55 kilometers per hour.

(3) Other motor vehicles not specified in (1) or (2), or motorcycles, shall be driven within the Bangkok Metropolitan Area, Pattaya City Area, or municipal areas at a speed not exceeding 80 kilometers per hour, or outside such areas at a speed not exceeding 70 kilometers per hour.

On roadways with traffic signs indicating a danger zone or a slow-driving zone, speed shall be reduced and caution increased as appropriate. In cases where traffic signs prescribe a speed limit lower than those specified above, the speed shall not exceed the speed limit so prescribed.

The Highway Act B.E. 2535 empowers the Minister to issue ministerial regulations prescribing speed limits for vehicles traveling on each category of highway, namely: the Ministerial Regulation Prescribing Speed Limits for Vehicles on Designated National Highways or Rural Highways B.E. 2564, which prescribes speed limits for vehicles on national highways or rural highways that have carriageways with at least two lanes in the same direction, a wall-type central median, and no at-grade U-turn points, as follows:

(1) Trucks with a vehicle weight exceeding 2,200 kilograms, or passenger vehicles with seating for more than fifteen passengers, shall travel at a speed not exceeding 90 kilometers per hour.

(2) Vehicles while towing other vehicles, small four-wheeled vehicles, or three-wheeled motor vehicles, shall travel at a speed not exceeding 65 kilometers per hour.

(3) Motorcycles shall travel at a speed not exceeding 80 kilometers per hour, except motorcycles with engine power of 35 kilowatts or more or with a combined cylinder displacement of 400 cubic centimeters or more, which may travel at a speed not exceeding 110 kilometers per hour.

(4) School buses or student transport vehicles shall travel at a speed not exceeding 80 kilometers per hour.

(5) Passenger vehicles with seating for more than seven but not more than fifteen passengers shall travel at a speed not exceeding 100 kilometers per hour.

(6) Tractors, road rollers, or agricultural vehicles shall travel at a speed not exceeding 45 kilometers per hour.

(7) Vehicles other than those in (1), (2), (3), (4), (5), and (6) shall travel at a speed not exceeding 120 kilometers per hour. In this regard, if such vehicle is in the rightmost lane, it must travel at a speed not less than 100 kilometers per hour, except where that lane has traffic restrictions, limited visibility, obstructions, or other impediments.

Clause 4: On roadways with traffic signs indicating a danger zone or a slow-driving zone, speed shall be reduced and caution increased as appropriate.

Clause 5: In cases where any roadway or traffic lane has traffic signs prescribing a speed limit lower than the rate prescribed in Clause 3, the speed shall not exceed the speed limit so prescribed.

3) Load Weight

The Highway Act B.E. 2535 empowers the Director of Highways for each category to issue announcements prohibiting the use of vehicles on highways where such vehicles have a weight, load weight, or axle weight exceeding the prescribed limits, or where such vehicles may cause damage to the highway. Violators shall be liable to imprisonment not exceeding 6 months or a fine not exceeding 10,000 baht, or both.

140.section: "Intersection" means the area where two or more roadways cross, converge, join, or adjoin each other.
140.body:
"Shoulder" means the area extending from the edge of the roadway outward to the side, which has not yet been constructed as a sidewalk.

"Intersection" means the area where two or more roadways cross, converge, join, or adjoin each other.

"Roundabout" means a roadway designated for vehicles to travel around a traffic sign or a structure built at an intersection.

"Sidewalk" means the area designated for pedestrians, located on one or both sides of the road, or the portion adjacent to the road edge used for pedestrian walking.

"Crosswalk" means the area designated for pedestrians to cross the road, marked with lines, markings, or studs on the road, and shall also include areas provided for pedestrians to cross whether at, below, or above ground level.

"Safety zone" means an area in the roadway that is clearly marked and visible at all times, designated for pedestrians crossing the road to stop and wait, or for persons boarding or alighting from vehicles to stop and wait before continuing to cross.

"Congested area" means a road with heavy traffic or obstructions, or a place where it can be foreseen that danger or damage to vehicles or persons may easily occur.

"Vehicle" means all types of land vehicles, except trains and trams.

"Motor vehicle" means a vehicle with three or more wheels that is propelled by engine power, electric power, or other energy, excluding vehicles that run on rails.

"Motorcycle" means a vehicle propelled by engine power, electric power, or other energy, having no more than two wheels; if a sidecar is attached, it may have no more than one additional wheel.

"Bicycle" means a vehicle propelled by the power of the rider, not being a vehicle that is dragged or pushed.

"Emergency vehicle" means fire engines and ambulances of the central government administration, regional government administration, and local government administration, or other vehicles authorized by the Director General to use flashing light signals or siren signals or other signals as may be prescribed.

"Truck" means a motor vehicle constructed for transporting goods or animals.

"Passenger vehicle" means a motor vehicle constructed for carrying more than 7 passengers.

"School bus" means a passenger vehicle used by a school to pick up and drop off students.

"Public bus" means a passenger vehicle that operates along a designated route and collects fares per person at rates set by distance or for the entire route.

"Taxi" means a motor vehicle used for hire to carry no more than 7 passengers.

"Tow truck" means a motor vehicle constructed for towing vehicles, agricultural equipment, or construction equipment, where the vehicle itself is not used for carrying persons or goods.

"Trailer" means a vehicle that is moved by being towed by another vehicle.

"Taximeter" means a device that displays the rate and fare of a taxi based on distance, time of taxi use, or both distance and time of taxi use.

"Driver" means a person who drives a vehicle, a person operating transport equipment under the law on transport, or a person dragging or pushing a vehicle.

"Pedestrian" means a person walking, and shall also include a person using a wheelchair for the disabled or a baby carriage.

"Vehicle owner" shall also include a person who has possession of the vehicle.

"Fare collector" means a person responsible for collecting fares and a person supervising passengers who is stationed on a passenger vehicle.

141.body:
"Driving license" means a motor vehicle driving license under the law on motor vehicles, a driver's license under the law on vehicles for hire, a driving license under the law on wheeled carts, and a transport equipment operator's license under the law on transport.

"Traffic signal" means any signal, whether displayed by flag, light, electric light, hand, arm, whistle, or by any other method, for drivers, pedestrians, or persons leading, riding, or herding animals to comply with such signal.

"Traffic sign" means any sign that has been installed or made to appear on a road for drivers, pedestrians, or persons leading, riding, or herding animals to comply with such sign.

"Inspector" means an inspector under the law on land transport and an inspector under the law on motor vehicles.

• Important Traffic Laws That Drivers Should Know

**Use of Vehicles**

Section 6: No person shall use on a traffic road any vehicle that is not in a stable and sturdy condition, or that may cause danger, or that may be detrimental to the health of users, passengers, or the public.

For vehicles used on traffic roads, the driver must ensure that the engine, equipment, and/or components are complete in accordance with the law on motor vehicles, the law on transport, the law on wheeled carts, the law on towed vehicles, or the law on vehicles for hire, and are in good working condition.

The condition of vehicles that may be detrimental to health under paragraph one and the testing methods shall be in accordance with the criteria and procedures prescribed in the ministerial regulation.

Section 7: No person shall use on a traffic road any vehicle that does not have a registration plate, registration mark plate, or vehicle identification plate affixed in accordance with the law on motor vehicles, the law on transport, the law on wheeled carts, the law on towed vehicles, or the law on vehicles for hire.

142.body:
Section 8: No person shall use on a road any vehicle from which the driver cannot see the road sufficiently for safety. For the purposes of this section, the Director-General shall have the power to issue regulations concerning the use of light-filtering materials on vehicles used on roads, to be published in the Government Gazette.

Section 9: No person shall use on a road any vehicle that produces excessive noise or has any part dragging on the road surface.

Section 10: No person shall use on a road any vehicle whose wheels or parts in contact with the road surface are not made of rubber, unless it is a vehicle exempted as prescribed in a ministerial regulation or a vehicle permitted by the chief traffic officer.

Section 10 bis: No person shall use on a road any vehicle whose engine produces gas, dust, smoke, chemical mist, or noise exceeding the standards prescribed by the Director-General by announcement published in the Government Gazette.

**Use of Lights or Sound Signals of Vehicles**

Section 11: When there is insufficient light to clearly see persons, vehicles, or obstructions on the road within a distance of not less than one hundred and fifty meters, a driver driving on a road must turn on lights or use illumination of the type, characteristics, and conditions prescribed in a ministerial regulation.

Section 12: For each type of vehicle used on a road, the driver must use the following specific sound signals:

(1) A horn, for motor vehicles or motorcycles, audible at a distance of not less than sixty meters;

(2) A bell, for horse-drawn carriages, audible at a distance of not less than thirty meters;

(3) A bicycle bell, for bicycles, audible at a distance of not less than thirty meters.

For vehicles other than those mentioned above, the driver must use sound signals as prescribed by the Director-General by announcement published in the Government Gazette.

Section 13: No driver of any type of vehicle on a road shall use flashing light signals, siren sound signals, whistle sound signals, cracked sounds, multiple-tone sounds, excessively loud sounds, or any other sound signals as prescribed by the Director-General by announcement published in the Government Gazette.

The Commissioner-General of the Royal Thai Police shall have the power to permit emergency vehicles, military or police vehicles, or other vehicles to use flashing light signals, siren sound signals, or other sound signals. In this regard, the Commissioner-General of the Royal Thai Police may also prescribe conditions for the use of light signals or sound signals, as well as prescribe markings indicating the characteristics of such vehicles, by announcement published in the Government Gazette.

Section 14: The use of sound signals by a driver is permitted only when necessary or to prevent accidents, and prolonged or excessively repeated use is not permitted.

The use of sound signals of vehicles or the prescription of conditions for the use of sound signals in any zone or area shall be determined by the Commissioner-General of the Royal Thai Police by announcement published in the Government Gazette.

Section 15: A vehicle carrying a load extending beyond the length of the vehicle, while on a road and during the time when lights must be turned on under Section 11 or Section 61, the driver must display a red light signal, or during daytime must attach a red flag at the outermost end of the load, with the light signal or flag visible at a distance of not less than one hundred and fifty meters.

The type, characteristics, or number of red light signals or red flags under paragraph one shall be prescribed by the Commissioner-General of the Royal Thai Police by announcement published in the Government Gazette.

143.body:
Section 16. A driver driving a vehicle transporting flammable liquids with a flash point at a temperature of twenty-one degrees Celsius or lower, or transporting flammable gas, must comply with Section 15 and Section 56, but the signal lights used must not be of the fuel-burning type.

Section 17. A driver driving a vehicle used for transporting explosives or any other type of hazardous materials must provide signs indicating the materials being transported and fire extinguishers, and must comply with the conditions for hazard prevention.

The format and method of displaying signs indicating the materials being transported and fire extinguishers, as well as the conditions for hazard prevention, shall be as prescribed in the ministerial regulations.

**Loading**

Section 18. Vehicles used for transporting persons, animals, or goods—the manner in which they may be loaded and by which type or category of vehicle—shall be in accordance with the criteria and methods prescribed in the ministerial regulations.

Section 19. In cases where it is necessary to transport persons, animals, or goods beyond the criteria and methods prescribed in the ministerial regulations, upon request by the vehicle owner, the traffic officer may grant a temporary written exemption on a case-by-case basis.

Section 20. A driver driving a vehicle transporting persons, animals, or goods must provide safeguards to prevent persons, animals, or goods being transported from falling off, leaking, emitting odors, reflecting light, or blowing off the vehicle, which may cause nuisance, make the road dirty or soiled, be detrimental to public health, or cause danger to persons or property.

**Driving**

Section 31. Except as specifically provided in Chapter 4 regarding the use of roads designated as bus lanes, the use of roads shall be in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.

Section 32. In using the road, a driver must exercise caution not to collide with or strike pedestrians regardless of what part of the road they may be on, and must give warning signals to alert pedestrians when necessary. In particular, when children, the elderly, or disabled persons are using the road, the driver must exercise special caution in controlling the vehicle.

Section 33. When driving, a driver must drive on the left side of the road and must not cross the center line of the road, except in the following cases where driving on the right side or crossing the center line of the road is permitted:

1) The left side of the road has an obstruction or is closed to traffic.
2) The road has been designated by the chief traffic officer as a one-way road.
3) The road is less than six meters wide.

144.section: 1) There is an obstruction in that lane or the lane is closed to traffic.
144.body:
Section 34: When using a roadway that has been divided into two or more lanes in the same direction, or where a bus lane has been designated in the leftmost lane, the driver must drive in the leftmost lane or the lane nearest to the bus lane, except in the following cases, where driving on the right side of the roadway is permitted:

1) There is an obstruction in that lane or the lane is closed to traffic.
2) The chief traffic officer has designated that roadway as a one-way road.
3) The driver must enter the correct lane when approaching the vicinity of an intersection.
4) When overtaking another vehicle.
5) When the driver is driving at a speed higher than vehicles in the left lane.

Section 35: A vehicle that is slow or traveling at a speed lower than other vehicles driving in the same direction — the driver must drive as close to the left edge of the roadway as practicable. Drivers of trucks, passenger transport vehicles, and motorcycles on a roadway that has been divided into two or more lanes in the same direction, or where a bus lane has been designated on the left side, must drive in the leftmost lane or the lane nearest to the bus lane, as the case may be.

The provisions of paragraph two shall not apply to private trucks weighing not more than one thousand six hundred kilograms and private passenger vehicles seating more than seven persons under the law on motor vehicles.

145.body:
Section 36: A driver who intends to turn a vehicle, allow another vehicle to pass or overtake, change a traffic lane, reduce the speed of the vehicle, park, or stop the vehicle must give a signal by hand and arm in accordance with Section 37, or a light signal in accordance with Section 38, or other signals in accordance with the regulations of the chief traffic officer.

If, due to the condition of the vehicle, the condition of the load, or visibility conditions, the hand and arm signal under paragraph one cannot be seen by a driver driving in the opposite direction or following behind, the driver must use a light signal.

The driver must give a signal by hand and arm, light signal, or other signal under paragraph one before turning the vehicle, changing a traffic lane, parking, or stopping the vehicle at a distance of not less than thirty meters.

The driver must give a signal by hand and arm, light signal, or other signal under paragraph one so that it is visible to other drivers at a distance of not less than sixty meters.

Section 37: Hand and arm signals shall be given as follows:

(1) When reducing the speed of the vehicle, the driver shall extend the right arm straight out of the vehicle at shoulder level and wave the hand up and down several times.

(2) When stopping the vehicle, the driver shall extend the right arm straight out of the vehicle at shoulder level, raise the lower right arm perpendicular to the upper arm, and hold the palm upward.

(3) When allowing another vehicle to pass or overtake, the driver shall extend the right arm straight out of the vehicle at shoulder level and wave the hand forward several times.

(4) When turning right or changing to a traffic lane on the right, the driver shall extend the right arm straight out of the vehicle at shoulder level.

(5) When turning left or changing to a traffic lane on the left, the driver shall extend the right arm straight out of the vehicle at shoulder level and bend the wrist upward, waving it to the left several times.

For the purposes of this section, in the case where the vehicle has the steering mechanism on the left side, the driver shall use light signals in place of hand and arm signals.

146.section: Section 38. The use of light signals by drivers of motor vehicles or motorcycles shall be as follows:
146.body:
Section 38. The use of light signals by drivers of motor vehicles or motorcycles shall be as follows:

(1) When stopping the vehicle, the driver must activate a red signal light at the rear of the vehicle.

(2) When turning, changing lanes, or overtaking another vehicle, the driver must activate an amber turn signal, or a flashing white or amber signal light installed at the front or side of the vehicle, and a flashing red or amber signal light installed at the rear of the vehicle, in the direction of the turn, lane change, or overtaking.

(3) When allowing another vehicle to overtake, the driver must activate an amber turn signal, or a flashing red or amber signal light installed at the rear of the vehicle on the left side of the vehicle.

Section 39. When driving in opposite directions, drivers shall keep to the left side of the roadway, using the center of the roadway as the reference point. However, if the roadway has been divided into traffic lanes, the dividing lines or markings shall be used as the reference point.

On narrow roadways when driving in opposite directions, drivers on each side must reduce speed to allow vehicles to pass each other safely.

On narrow roadways where vehicles cannot pass each other safely, when driving in opposite directions, the driver of the larger vehicle must stop close to the left edge of the roadway to allow the driver of the smaller vehicle to pass.

On roadways with an obstruction ahead, the driver must reduce speed or stop the vehicle to allow the oncoming vehicle to pass.

Section 40. A driver must maintain a sufficient distance from the vehicle ahead to be able to stop safely when it is necessary to stop.

A driver driving up a bridge or on a steep incline must exercise caution to prevent the vehicle from rolling backward into another vehicle.

Section 41. On any roadway where traffic signs designate it as a one-way roadway, drivers shall drive in the direction specified.

147.section: Section 43: A driver is prohibited from driving a vehicle:

148.body:
Section 43 quater: In the event that an inspector finds that any driver has violated Section 43 (1) or (2) or Section 43 bis, paragraph one, the inspector shall deliver that person together with preliminary evidence to the competent inquiry official without delay, but no later than six hours from the time the said offense was discovered, for further criminal proceedings.

Section 43 quinquies: In performing duties under Section 43 bis and Section 43 ter, the inspector shall present his or her identification card issued under the law on land transport or the law on motor vehicles to the persons concerned.

**Overtaking and Passing**

14

Section 44: A driver who wishes to overtake another vehicle on a roadway where traffic lanes are not divided must signal by flashing the headlights several times, or activating the right turn signal, or sounding the horn loud enough for the driver of the vehicle ahead to give a responding signal pursuant to Section 37 (3) or Section 38 (3), and when it is apparent that it will not obstruct other vehicles that are overtaking, the driver may then overtake.

Overtaking must be done on the right side, maintaining a reasonable distance from the vehicle being overtaken. Only when the driver is satisfied that he or she has passed the overtaken vehicle at a sufficient distance may the driver move back to the left side of the roadway.

Section 45: No driver shall overtake another vehicle on the left side, except in the following cases:

(1) The vehicle to be overtaken is turning right or signaling a right turn.

(2) The roadway is divided into two or more lanes for traffic traveling in the same direction.

Overtaking on the left under (1) or (2) may be done only when no other vehicle is following closely behind and it is sufficiently safe.

Section 46: No driver shall overtake another vehicle in the following cases:

(1) When the vehicle is going uphill, ascending a bridge, or on a curve, unless there is a traffic sign permitting overtaking.

(2) Within thirty meters before reaching a crossing, a junction, an intersection, a roundabout, a traffic island, or a roadway crossing a railway.

(3) When fog, rain, dust, or smoke reduces visibility ahead to less than sixty meters.

(4) When entering a narrow passage or a safety zone.

Section 47: No driver shall overtake or pass another vehicle by encroaching beyond the center line of the roadway as designated, or where there are traffic signs indicating a danger zone or a zone requiring caution on the roadway.

In the event that the left side of the roadway has an obstruction impeding traffic and the right side of the roadway is sufficiently wide, the driver may drive past the obstruction by encroaching beyond the center line of the roadway designated by the traffic official, provided that it does not obstruct traffic coming from the opposite direction.

15

149.body:
Section 48: A driver shall not overtake or pass another vehicle by encroaching into the bus lane, except in cases where there is an obstruction to traffic on the road ahead or when complying with an order of the chief traffic officer. In any case, the driver may drive in the bus lane only to the extent necessary.

Section 49: Upon receiving a signal requesting to overtake from a vehicle behind, a driver who is driving a slow vehicle or a vehicle traveling at a speed lower than that of other vehicles traveling in the same direction must allow the faster vehicle to pass ahead. The driver who is requested to give way must give a responding signal in accordance with Section 37 (3) or Section 38 (3). When it is apparent that the road ahead is safe and there is no oncoming vehicle approaching at close range, the driver must reduce speed and drive close to the left side of the road to allow the overtaking vehicle to pass ahead safely.

**Starting, Turning, and Making U-Turns**

Section 50: When driving a vehicle out of a parking space, if there is a parked vehicle or an obstruction ahead, the driver must give a signal by hand and arm in accordance with Section 37 or by signal lights in accordance with Section 38, and may proceed only when it is safe and does not obstruct the traffic of other vehicles.

Section 51: Turning a vehicle shall be carried out as follows:

(1) If turning left:

(a) In cases where traffic lanes are not designated, the driver shall drive close to the left side of the road.

(b) In cases where traffic lanes are designated and there is a traffic sign indicating that a left turn is permitted, the driver shall drive in the lane designated for left-turning vehicles no less than thirty meters before reaching the turn.

(c) In cases where there is a bus lane on the far left side of the road, the driver shall drive close to the bus lane no less than thirty meters before reaching the turn, and may turn through the bus lane only in areas where traffic signs permit turning through it.

150.body:
(2) If turning right:

(a) For roads where traffic lanes are not divided, the driver shall drive close to the right side of the center line of the road not less than thirty meters before reaching the turn.

(b) For roads where traffic lanes in the same direction are divided into two or more lanes, the driver shall drive in the rightmost lane of the road or in the lane with a traffic sign indicating a right turn is permitted, not less than thirty meters before reaching the turn.

(c) In cases where there is a bus lane on the rightmost side of the road, the driver shall drive close to the bus lane not less than thirty meters before reaching the turn, and may turn through the bus lane only in areas where traffic signs permit turning through.

(d) For roads where a traffic officer or authorized official is directing traffic by hand and arm signals, the driver may turn right without having to go around the traffic officer or authorized official; the driver shall pass through the intersection first and, when it is seen to be safe, may then turn right.

(3) If turning around a roundabout or traffic island constructed therein, the driver shall drive around to the left of the roundabout or island.

In the cases under (1) and (2), the driver must exercise caution and must stop to give way to persons crossing the road and vehicles passing through the intersection from other directions first, except in cases where vehicles are turning left and turning right simultaneously, in which case the vehicle turning left shall give way to the vehicle turning right first.

Section 52: On roads where traffic can travel in both directions, no driver shall make a U-turn or turn right when another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction or following from behind at a distance of less than one hundred meters, unless it is seen to be safe and does not obstruct the traffic of other vehicles.

Section 53: No driver shall:

(1) Turn or make a U-turn on a road where there is a no right turn, no left turn, or no U-turn sign.

(2) Make a U-turn at a safety zone, at a narrow passage, on a bridge, or within one hundred meters from the level approach of a bridge.

(3) Make a U-turn at an intersection, unless there is a traffic sign permitting a U-turn in such area.

151.body:
**Stopping and Parking**

**Section 54** When stopping or parking on a roadway, the driver must give a hand and arm signal in accordance with Section 37 or a light signal in accordance with Section 38 at a distance of not less than thirty meters before stopping or parking, and may stop or park only when the driver sees that it is safe and does not obstruct traffic. The driver must park on the left side of the roadway and park with the left side of the vehicle parallel to and close to the road edge or road shoulder at a distance of not more than twenty-five centimeters, or park in the direction or on the side of the roadway designated by the chief traffic officer. However, in cases where there is a bus lane on the leftmost side of the roadway, the driver is prohibited from parking in such manner during the time designated for use of that bus lane.

**Section 55** Drivers are prohibited from stopping a vehicle:

(1) In a traffic lane, except when stopping close to the left edge of the roadway in cases where there is no bus lane.

(2) On a sidewalk.

(3) On a bridge or in a tunnel.

(4) At an intersection.

(5) In an area with a no-stopping traffic sign.

(6) Directly at the entrance or exit of a building or roadway.

(7) In a safety zone.

(8) In a manner that obstructs traffic.

The provisions of the first paragraph shall not apply to a driver who must stop the vehicle due to an obstruction on the roadway, or due to engine or vehicle equipment malfunction, or in cases of compliance with traffic signals or traffic signs.

**Section 56** In cases where the engine or vehicle equipment malfunctions requiring the vehicle to be parked on the roadway, the driver must move the vehicle off the roadway as quickly as possible. In the case under the first paragraph, if it is necessary to park the vehicle on the roadway, the driver must park in a manner that does not obstruct traffic and must display markings or signals in accordance with the characteristics and conditions prescribed in the ministerial regulation.

**Section 57** Unless otherwise provided by provisions, rules, or regulations under this Act, drivers are prohibited from parking:

(1) On a sidewalk.

(2) On a bridge or in a tunnel.

(3) At an intersection or within ten meters of an intersection.

(4) At a crosswalk or within three meters of a crosswalk.

(5) In an area with a no-parking traffic sign.

(6) Within three meters of a fire hydrant.

(7) Within ten meters of a traffic signal installation.

(8) Within fifteen meters of a railway crossing.

(9) Double-parked alongside another vehicle already parked.

(10) Directly at the entrance or exit of a building or roadway, or within five meters of a roadway entrance.

(11) Between a safety zone and the road edge, or within ten meters from either end of the safety zone.

(12) In a narrow or confined area.

153.section: **Use of Roadways Designated as Bus Lanes**
153.body:
Section 63: On any section of a roadway where a railway crosses, whether or not there is a railway warning sign, if that railway crossing has no railway warning signal or barrier, the driver must reduce speed and stop the vehicle at a distance of not less than five meters from the railway. The driver may proceed only when it is seen to be safe.

Section 64: While a school bus driver has stopped the vehicle on a roadway to pick up or drop off students, drivers of other vehicles following in the same direction or traveling in the opposite direction of the school bus shall exercise caution and reduce speed. They may proceed past only when it is seen to be safe.

**Use of Roadways Designated as Bus Lanes**

Section 65: When the chief traffic officer has announced the designation of any traffic lane as a bus lane, drivers of regular bus services and passenger transport vehicles of the type designated by the Commissioner-General of the Royal Thai Police, while in the course of picking up, dropping off, or carrying passengers, must drive within the bus lane. They may drive out of the bus lane only when there is an obstruction in the bus lane or when complying with the order of a traffic officer.

The types of passenger transport vehicles required to travel in the bus lane shall be as determined by the Commissioner-General of the Royal Thai Police and published in the Government Gazette.

In announcing the designation of any traffic lane as a bus lane under paragraph one, the hours of use of the bus lane may also be specified.

In cases of traffic necessity, the chief traffic officer has the authority to announce that passenger transport vehicles of any type designated by the Commissioner-General of the Royal Thai Police under paragraph two must travel in the bus lane on any route or any section thereof.

Section 66: No driver of any vehicle other than a regular bus service or a passenger transport vehicle of the type designated by the Commissioner-General of the Royal Thai Police shall drive in a bus lane, unless acting in compliance with the provisions of this Act.

**Provisions Regarding Vehicle Speed**

Section 67: A driver must drive at the speed prescribed in the ministerial regulation or as indicated by traffic signs installed on the road. Traffic signs installed under paragraph one may prescribe maximum or minimum speed limits, but shall not exceed the speed prescribed in the ministerial regulation.

Section 68: A driver who is turning, allowing another vehicle to overtake or pass, parking, stopping, or making a U-turn must reduce the speed of the vehicle.

Section 69: A driver driving on a roadway on a hill, on a bridge, at the foot of a bridge, on a narrow road, on a curve, on a slope, in a confined area, or where fog, rain, dust, or smoke reduces visibility ahead to less than sixty meters must reduce speed in a manner that ensures safety.

Section 70: A driver approaching an intersection, a crosswalk, a stop line, or a roundabout must reduce the speed of the vehicle.

154.body:
**Driving Through Intersections or Roundabouts**

**Section 71** Subject to Section 21 and Section 26, when a driver drives to an intersection, the driver shall comply as follows:

1) If there is another vehicle in the intersection, the driver must allow the vehicle in the intersection to pass first.

2) If vehicles arrive at the intersection at the same time and there is no vehicle in the intersection, the driver must allow the vehicle on one's left side to pass first, except where a major route crosses a minor route at the intersection, in which case the driver driving on the major route shall have the right to pass first.

3) If a green traffic signal light appears ahead but there is another vehicle stopped and blocking the intersection such that it is not possible to pass through the intersection, the driver must stop behind the stop line until the vehicle can move through and clear the intersection.

**Section 72** A major route refers to the following routes:

(1) A route where traffic signs have been installed indicating that it is a major route.

(2) A route where a stop sign or a sign bearing the words "Give Way" (ให้ทาง) has been installed, or a route where the word "Stop" (หยุด) or a stop line which is a solid white line, or a give-way line which is a dashed white line is marked on the road surface — the route crossing ahead shall be deemed a major route.

(3) In cases where there are no traffic signs under (1) or no signs, lines, or text on the road surface under (2), the route with more traffic lanes shall be deemed the major route.

(4) A road that intersects or joins with a lane or alley (soi) — the route that is the road shall be deemed the major route.

Any route other than a major route under paragraph one shall be a minor route.

**Section 73** In cases where traffic signals or traffic signs have been installed at any roundabout, the driver must comply with such traffic signals or traffic signs. If there are no traffic signals or traffic signs under paragraph one, when a driver drives to a roundabout, the driver must give right of way to the driver driving in the roundabout on one's right side to pass first.

In cases where a traffic officer deems it appropriate for the safety or convenience of traffic, the officer may give traffic signals other than those prescribed in paragraph one or paragraph two. In such cases, the driver must comply with the traffic signals designated by the traffic officer.

**Section 74** A driver driving a vehicle out of a private road or a roadway within a building compound, when driving through or turning onto a crossing roadway, must stop the vehicle to allow vehicles passing through or vehicles traveling on the roadway to pass first. The driver may proceed only when it is deemed safe.

**Emergency Vehicles**

**Section 75** While a driver is driving an emergency vehicle in the performance of duty, the driver shall have the following rights:

(1) To use flashing light signals, siren sound signals, or other sound signals as designated by the Commissioner-General of the Royal Thai Police.

(2) To stop or park the vehicle at places where parking is prohibited.

(3) To drive in excess of the prescribed speed limit.

(4) To drive through any traffic signal or traffic sign requiring vehicles to stop, but must reduce the speed of the vehicle to a reasonably slow pace.

(5) Not to comply with the provisions of this Act or traffic regulations concerning traffic lanes, direction of driving, or turning as prescribed.

In exercising the rights under paragraph one, the driver must exercise due caution as appropriate to the circumstances.

159.body:
Section 122. A motorcycle driver and a motorcycle passenger must wear a helmet specifically made for protection against danger while driving and riding a motorcycle. The motorcycle driver under paragraph one is prohibited from driving a motorcycle while the motorcycle passenger is not wearing a helmet specifically made for protection against danger. The characteristics and method of using a protective helmet under paragraph one shall be in accordance with the ministerial regulations. The provisions of paragraph one shall not apply to monks, novices, ascetics, clergy, or followers of other religions who wear cloth or other head coverings according to their customary traditions, or any persons specified in the ministerial regulations.

Section 123. No driver of a motor vehicle shall allow more than two other persons to sit in the front row seat alongside the driver's seat. The motor vehicle driver must fasten the body with a seatbelt to the seat while driving, and must ensure that passengers sitting in the front row seat alongside the driver's seat fasten their bodies to the seat with a seatbelt while riding, and such passengers must also fasten their bodies with a seatbelt to the seat while riding. The type or kind of motor vehicle, and the characteristics and method of using seatbelts under paragraph two, shall be in accordance with what the Commissioner-General of the Royal Thai Police prescribes, as published in the Government Gazette.

Section 124. No person shall do anything that causes the driver to be unable to see the front or sides of the vehicle conveniently while driving, or in a manner that obstructs the control of the vehicle. No person shall cling to, hang from, or extend any part of the body outside the body of a motor vehicle unnecessarily, or sit or stand in or on a motor vehicle in a manner that may cause danger while the motor vehicle is moving on a carriageway. No person shall board or alight from a regular bus, passenger transport vehicle, school bus, or taxi while such vehicle is stopped waiting for a traffic light signal or stopped due to traffic congestion. No driver or fare collector of a regular bus, passenger transport vehicle, school bus, or taxi shall allow any person to do anything under paragraph two or paragraph three.

Section 125. When driving through a narrow road between mountains or between hills, or when driving on a carriageway on a mountain or on a hill, the driver must drive close to the left edge of the road, and upon reaching a curve, the driver must use a horn signal to warn other vehicles that may be approaching from the opposite direction.

Section 126. No driver shall use neutral gear or depress the clutch while driving down a slope or a hillside.

Section 127. No driver shall drive a vehicle:
(1) following behind an emergency vehicle that is performing its duties at a distance of less than fifty meters;
(2) entering or parking in a fire-fighting operation zone;
(3) over a fire hose that has no hose protection device while firefighting personnel are performing their duties, unless consent is obtained from the firefighting personnel on duty at that time.

Section 128. No person shall place, pour, or discard broken glass, nails, wire, lubricating oil, cans, or any other objects, or do anything on a road that may cause danger or damage to vehicles or persons, or obstruct traffic.

Section 129. Any person who knows that any object under Section 128 that is under their care has fallen, spilled, or flowed onto the road must immediately collect and sweep such objects off the road.

161.section: The Road Traffic Act B.E. 2522 has stipulated the practices related to traffic light signals as follows:
161.body:
The Road Traffic Act B.E. 2522 has stipulated the practices related to traffic light signals as follows:

Section 22: A driver must comply with the traffic signal or traffic sign appearing ahead in the following cases:

1) Amber yellow traffic light signal: The driver shall prepare to stop the vehicle behind the stop line in order to prepare to comply with the signal that will appear next as stated in (2), except for a driver who has already passed the stop line, who may proceed.

2) Red traffic light signal, or a red traffic sign bearing the word "Stop."

3) Green traffic light signal, or a green traffic sign bearing the word "Go": The driver may proceed, unless a traffic sign specifies otherwise.

4) Green arrow traffic light signal indicating a turn or indicating to go straight, or a red traffic light signal displayed simultaneously with a green arrow traffic light signal indicating a turn or indicating to go straight: The driver may turn or drive straight ahead in the direction indicated by the arrow, and must drive with caution and give right of way to pedestrians in the crosswalk or vehicles coming from the right. The driver shall stop the vehicle behind the stop line.

5) Flashing red traffic light signal: If installed at any intersection on any approach, the driver approaching from that direction shall stop the vehicle behind the stop line. When it is seen to be safe and not obstructing traffic, the driver may then proceed with caution.

6) Flashing amber yellow traffic light signal: If installed at any location, the driver shall reduce the speed of the vehicle and pass through that traffic lane with caution.

A driver intending to go straight must position the vehicle in the traffic lane marked with a traffic sign indicating to go straight. A driver intending to turn must position the vehicle in the traffic lane marked with a traffic sign indicating a turn. Entry into such traffic lane must be made from the point where the traffic sign indicating such action first appears.

162.body:
2) Hand Signals

Hand signals, or signals using the hands and arms of a traffic officer, refer to traffic signals that an officer displays visibly ahead.

The Road Traffic Act B.E. 2522, Section 24, stipulates that drivers must comply with traffic signals displayed by traffic officers in the following cases:

1. When a traffic officer stands and extends the left arm out at shoulder level, drivers approaching from behind the officer must stop their vehicles. However, if the officer lowers the extended arm and waves the hand forward, drivers who have stopped behind may proceed.

2. When a traffic officer stands and extends either arm out at shoulder level with the palm raised upright, drivers approaching from the side of that extended arm must stop their vehicles. However, if the officer flips the raised palm and waves it over the head toward the rear, drivers who have stopped may proceed.

3. When a traffic officer stands and extends both arms out at shoulder level with both palms raised upright, drivers approaching from the side of both extended arms must stop their vehicles.

4. When a traffic officer stands and raises the right forearm perpendicular to the upper arm with the palm raised upright, drivers approaching from the front of the officer must stop their vehicles. However, if the officer flips the raised palm and waves it toward the rear, drivers who have stopped in front of the officer may proceed.

163.body:
5. When a traffic officer stands with the right forearm raised perpendicular to the upper arm with the palm facing up, and the left arm extended out at shoulder level, drivers approaching from the front and the rear of the officer must stop their vehicles.

**Stopping Distance**

Stopping under this section shall be behind the stop line. In the case where any roadway has no stop line, the driver shall stop the vehicle at a distance of not less than three meters from the traffic officer.

**When Hand Signals Differ from Traffic Light Signals**

On any roadway that has traffic light signals or traffic signs, if the traffic officer controlling traffic on that roadway deems it appropriate for the sake of safety or convenience of traffic, the officer may give a different traffic signal. In such a case, the driver shall operate the vehicle in accordance with the signal given by the traffic officer.

**3) Whistle Signals**

The street environment, with engine noise from various vehicles, is an obstacle to calling out or giving signals by spoken words. Therefore, traffic officers use whistle sounds as a tool for giving traffic signals.

The Road Traffic Act B.E. 2522, Section 25, prescribes the procedures requiring drivers to comply with traffic signals given by traffic officers using whistle signals in the following cases:

1. When a traffic officer blows one long whistle blast, the driver must stop the vehicle immediately.
2. When a traffic officer blows two short whistle blasts in succession, the driver may proceed.

164.body:
• **Traffic Signs**

**Traffic signs** mean images, text, letters, numbers, studs, posts, lines, colored strips, or any symbols that are displayed, installed, or made to appear within the road zone or highway in a manner and position that is easily and clearly visible, so that road users—whether drivers, pedestrians, or persons controlling animals—comply with the meaning of those signs, or to provide information or guidance regarding the use of that road or highway, in order to ensure that traffic flows smoothly, quickly, and safely.

Drivers operating vehicles on the road absolutely must have knowledge and understanding of the various traffic signs and markings in order to control their vehicles correctly and safely. Therefore, it is necessary to have knowledge and understanding of what to do when encountering traffic signal signs and traffic markings on the road.

Traffic signs are divided into **2 types**: sign-board traffic signs and road-surface/road-edge traffic markings.

**1. Sign-Board Traffic Signs**

Traffic signs that appear on sign boards, boxes, or panels made of metal sheets, wood, or other materials, divided into **3 categories** as follows:

• **Regulatory Signs** are traffic signs whose meaning compels road users to comply with the traffic sign displayed on that sign, by requiring road users to perform, refrain from performing, or restricting certain actions or behaviors, with the following meanings:

1) **"Stop" sign** means the driver must stop the vehicle before reaching the cross road ahead or the stop line, and wait for vehicles and/or pedestrians on the cross road ahead to pass first. When it is deemed safe and will not obstruct traffic at that intersection, the driver may then proceed with caution.

2) **"Yield" (Give Way) sign** means the driver must exercise caution and give way to vehicles or pedestrians on the cross road ahead to pass first. When it is deemed safe and will not obstruct traffic at that intersection, the driver may then proceed with caution.

3) **"Give Way to Oncoming Traffic" sign** means the driver must stop the vehicle at the position where the sign is installed and wait for oncoming vehicles to pass first. If there are vehicles ahead already waiting, the driver must stop in line behind them in order. Once all oncoming vehicles have passed, the vehicles stopped at this sign may then proceed.

4) **"No Overtaking" sign** means overtaking another vehicle is prohibited within the road zone where the sign is installed.

165.section: 5) "No Entry" sign means no vehicles of any kind are allowed to enter in the direction where the sign is installed.
165.body:
5) "No Entry" sign means no vehicles of any kind are allowed to enter in the direction where the sign is installed.

6) "No U-Turn to the Right" sign means making a U-turn to the right is prohibited by any means whatsoever.

7) "No U-Turn to the Left" sign means making a U-turn to the left is prohibited by any means whatsoever.

8) "No Left Turn" sign means turning the vehicle to the left is prohibited.

9) "No Right Turn" sign means turning the vehicle to the right is prohibited.

10) "No Changing Lanes to the Left" sign means changing the driving lane or traffic lane to the left is prohibited.

11) "No Changing Lanes to the Right" sign means changing the driving lane or traffic lane to the right is prohibited.

32

166.section: 12) "No Right Turn or U-Turn" sign means turning right or making a U-turn is prohibited.
166.body:
12) "No Right Turn or U-Turn" sign means turning right or making a U-turn is prohibited.

13) "No Left Turn or U-Turn" sign means turning left or making a U-turn is prohibited.

14) "No Motor Vehicles" sign means all types of motor vehicles are prohibited from passing in or out of the road zone where the sign is installed.

15) "No Trucks" sign means all types of trucks are prohibited from passing in or out of the road zone where the sign is installed.

16) "No Motorcycles" sign means all types of motorcycles are prohibited from passing in or out of the road zone where the sign is installed.

17) "No Trailers" sign means all types of trailers or semi-trailers are prohibited from passing in or out of the road zone where the sign is installed.

18) "No Three-Wheeled Motor Vehicles" sign means all types of three-wheeled motor vehicles are prohibited from passing in or out of the road zone where the sign is installed.

19) "No Tricycles" sign means all types of tricycles are prohibited from entering or exiting the road zone where the sign is installed.

• **Warning Signs**

Warning signs are traffic signs that serve to warn road users in advance of road conditions or other information occurring on the road or highway ahead that may cause danger or accidents, so that road users exercise caution when using the road, which can help prevent such accidents. Their meanings are as follows:

1) **"Various Curves"** sign means the road ahead is a curve as indicated by the arrow on the sign. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

- Warning Sign: Left Curve (ทางโค้งซ้าย)
- Warning Sign: Right Curve (ทางโค้งขวา)
- Warning Sign: Reverse Curve Starting Right (ทางโค้งกลับเริ่มขวา)
- Warning Sign: Reverse Curve Starting Left (ทางโค้งกลับเริ่มซ้าย)
- Warning Sign: Sharp Left Curve (ทางโค้งรัศมีแคบเลี้ยวซ้าย)
- Warning Sign: Sharp Right Curve (ทางโค้งรัศมีแคบเลี้ยวขวา)
- Warning Sign: Sharp Reverse Curve Left (ทางโค้งกลับรัศมีแคบเลี้ยวซ้าย)
- Warning Sign: Sharp Reverse Curve Right (ทางโค้งกลับรัศมีแคบเลี้ยวขวา)
- Warning Sign: Winding Road Starting Left (ทางคดเคี้ยวเริ่มซ้าย)
- Warning Sign: Winding Road Starting Right (ทางคดเคี้ยวเริ่มขวา)

174.body:
2) "Various Intersection" sign means the road ahead is an intersection as indicated by the symbol on the sign. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

Warning Sign: Major Roads Intersecting | Warning Sign: Major Roads Y-Intersection | Warning Sign: Minor Road Branches Left to Major Road | Warning Sign: Minor Road Branches Right to Major Road

Warning Sign: Minor Road Joins Major Road from Left | Warning Sign: Minor Road Joins Major Road from Right | Warning Sign: Minor Road Branches Right to Major Road Y-Intersection | Warning Sign: Minor Road Branches Left to Major Road Y-Intersection

Warning Sign: Minor Road Branches from Major Road Staggered Starting Right | Warning Sign: Minor Road Branches from Major Road Staggered Starting Left

3) "Roundabout Ahead" sign means the road ahead is an intersection with a roundabout. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

4) "Road Narrows on Both Sides" sign means the road ahead narrows on both sides compared to the current road. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

175.body:
5) The "Road Narrows on Left Side" sign means the road ahead narrows on the left side compared to the current road. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

6) The "Road Narrows on Right Side" sign means the road ahead narrows on the right side compared to the current road. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

7) The "Narrow Bridge" sign means the road ahead has a narrow bridge where it is not convenient for vehicles to pass each other. Drivers should slow down and beware of danger from vehicles coming from the other side of the bridge.

8) The "Left Lane Closed" sign means the traffic lane ahead is closed on the left side. Drivers should change to the remaining available lane(s) with caution.

9) The "Right Lane Closed" sign means the traffic lane ahead is closed on the right side. Drivers should change to the remaining available lane(s) with caution.

10) The "Railway Crossing Without Gate" sign means the road ahead has a railway crossing without a gate barrier. Drivers should slow down and look for trains in both the right and left directions. If a train is approaching, the driver should stop the vehicle at least 5 meters from the railway track and wait until the train has passed and it is safe before proceeding. Under no circumstances should a driver cut across in front of a train at a distance that could cause danger.

176.body:
11) The "Railway Crossing with Gate" sign means that the road ahead has a railway crossing with a barrier or gate. Before driving past this sign, drivers should slow down and be ready to stop when the officer's signal sounds or the officer closes the gate, or when the gate is closed. If there are vehicles already stopped ahead, stop and wait in line. Once the gate is opened, the waiting vehicles may proceed in order.

12) The "Railway Crossing Adjacent to Intersection" sign means that the road ahead has a railway crossing adjacent to an intersection as indicated by the symbol. Drivers should drive with caution. Before crossing the railway, look to the left and right along the railway tracks. When it is confirmed safe, proceed driving. In cases where there is a gate, drivers should comply with the gate signals.

13) The "Narrow Road" sign means that the road ahead is narrower than the current road, with the width specified in "meters" as indicated on the sign. Vehicles with a width not exceeding the number indicated on the sign may pass through. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

14) The "Low Underpass" sign means that the road ahead passes through a low underpass with a clearance specified in "meters" as indicated on the sign. Vehicles with a height, including loaded cargo, not exceeding the number indicated on the sign may pass through. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

15) The "Steep Ascent" sign means that the road ahead is a steep uphill road, going up a hill or slope, with a gradient specified as a "percentage" as indicated on the sign. The crest of the hill or slope may obstruct the view of oncoming vehicles. Drivers should slow down, keep as close to the left edge of the road as possible, and exercise caution against oncoming vehicles.

16) The "Steep Descent" sign means that the road ahead is a steep downhill road, going down a hill or slope, with a gradient specified as a "percentage" as indicated on the sign. Drivers should slow down, keep as close to the left edge of the road as possible, and use low gear for safety. Under no circumstances should the gear be disengaged or the engine turned off.

• Construction Zone Warning Signs

Construction zone warning signs have the following meanings:

1) "Road Survey" (สำรวจทาง) sign means that survey work is being conducted ahead on the road surface or carriageway, or near the road surface or carriageway. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

2) "Construction in Progress" (กำลังมีงานก่อสร้าง) sign means that construction work is being conducted ahead on the road surface or carriageway, or near the road surface or carriageway. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

3) "Workers Ahead" (คนทำงาน) sign means that there are workers ahead. Equipment or materials may be placed on the road surface or carriageway, or near the road surface or carriageway. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

4) "Machinery at Work" (เครื่องจักรกำลังทำงาน) sign means that machinery is operating ahead on the road surface or carriageway, or near the road surface or carriageway. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

5) "Left Detour" (ทางเบี่ยงซ้าย) sign means that there is construction work ahead and it is necessary to divert traffic to a detour or temporary road on the left side. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

6) "Right Detour" (ทางเบี่ยงขวา) sign means that there is construction work ahead and it is necessary to divert traffic to a detour or temporary road on the right side. Drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

186.body:
2. Road Surface Traffic Markings refer to traffic markings displayed on the road surface, carriageway, road shoulder, sidewalk, road edge, roundabout curb, or curb stone by using tiles, metal studs, reflective materials, paint, or any other materials through paving, nailing, embedding, spraying, painting, heat application, or any other method to display traffic markings. They are divided into 2 categories as follows:

• Regulatory Road Surface Traffic Markings

Regulatory road surface traffic markings are traffic markings that have a mandatory meaning requiring road users to comply with the meaning of such markings, by requiring road users to perform, refrain from performing, or restricting certain actions or certain manners, with the following meanings:

**Traffic Markings Along the Direction of Travel**

1. **Normal Traffic Direction Dividing Line** has the appearance of a yellow dashed line, meaning it is a line indicating the separation of traffic traveling in opposite directions. Drivers must drive on the left side of the line, except when making a right turn or overtaking another vehicle.

2. **No-Overtaking Traffic Direction Dividing Line** has the appearance of a single or double solid yellow line, meaning drivers must drive on the left side of the line and are strictly prohibited from driving across or straddling the line.

3. **One-Side No-Overtaking Traffic Direction Dividing Line** has the appearance of a solid yellow line paired with a dashed yellow line, meaning vehicles on the solid line side are strictly prohibited from crossing or straddling the solid line, while vehicles on the dashed line side, when it is deemed safe, may overtake another vehicle or cross such line with caution.

187.body:
4. **Lane dividing line or traffic lane dividing line** appears as a white dashed line dividing the roadway or traffic way traveling in the same direction into lanes or traffic lanes. This means the driver must drive within the lane or traffic lane and must not drive straddling the line, except when changing lanes or traffic lanes.

5. **No lane changing line or no traffic lane changing line** appears as a solid white line dividing the roadway or traffic way traveling in the same direction into lanes or traffic lanes. This means the driver must drive within the lane or traffic lane and must not drive across or straddle the line.

6. **Bus lane dividing line** appears as a wide and closely spaced yellow dashed line in the case of normal opposing traffic, and a wide and closely spaced white dashed line in the case of the same direction as normal traffic. It is accompanied by a yellow arrow and may include the words "รถประจำทาง" or "BUS" in yellow. This means it is a bus lane. Other types of vehicles are prohibited from entering the bus lane.

7. **No parking marking** appears as alternating yellow and white stripes displayed on the curb or road edge on the left side of the roadway or traffic way, or at other locations. This means parking of all types of vehicles is prohibited within the designated zone, except for briefly stopping to pick up or drop off passengers or goods, which must be done without delay.

8. **No stopping marking** appears as alternating red and white stripes displayed on the curb or road edge on the left side of the roadway or traffic way, or at other locations. This means stopping or parking of all types of vehicles within the designated zone is strictly prohibited.

188.body:
**Traffic Markings Across the Roadway**

1. **Stop Line** has the appearance of a wide solid white line across the roadway. This means that when a traffic signal commands a stop or there is a stop sign, the driver must stop the vehicle before reaching the stop line. When the traffic signal permits proceeding, or when it will not cause an obstruction to traffic, the driver may proceed past the stop line.

2. **Yield Line** has the appearance of a wide dashed white line across the roadway. This means the driver must slow down. If it appears that proceeding would be unsafe for other vehicles or pedestrians on the cross road ahead, or would obstruct traffic, the driver must stop the vehicle before reaching the yield line.

3. **Crosswalk Line** has the appearance of multiple wide, long white strips placed together across the roadway, or two solid white parallel lines across the roadway, accompanied by a stop line or yield line. This means the driver must slow down and be ready to stop the vehicle promptly when there are pedestrians crossing at that crosswalk. At crosswalks where there are no officers or traffic signals, pedestrians have the right to cross first. Therefore, while pedestrians are walking in the crosswalk, the driver must stop the vehicle before the stop line or yield line, and may proceed only after the pedestrians have finished crossing.

189.body:
4. **Diagonal No-Stopping Lines** (เส้นทแยงห้ามหยุดรถ) have the appearance of solid yellow diagonal lines crossing each other within a solid yellow border. This means that all types of vehicles are prohibited from stopping within the diagonal no-stopping zone, except for vehicles waiting to turn right.

**Other Markings**

1. **Arrows** have the appearance of white or yellow arrows indicating traffic directions for going straight, turning left, turning right, making a U-turn, or combinations thereof. This means that when they appear in a traffic lane or carriageway, drivers in that lane or carriageway must comply with those markings.

2. **Yield** (ให้ทาง) has the appearance of a white triangle with a pointed tip facing against the direction of traffic, displayed or marked on the road surface in conjunction with a yield line. This means that drivers must slow down. If it appears unsafe for other vehicles or pedestrians on the cross road ahead, or if it would obstruct traffic, drivers must stop before the yield line.

190.body:
3. **Safety Zone or Painted Island** has the appearance of strips or solid lines in white or yellow, drawn diagonally to the direction of traffic, or in a herringbone pattern, and surrounded by solid white or yellow lines. This means vehicles are prohibited from encroaching into such areas.

4. **High-Occupancy Vehicle Lane** has the appearance of a white diamond shape with its pointed ends aligned in the direction of traffic. Inside the diamond, there may be a number indicating the minimum number of occupants required in a high-occupancy vehicle. This means the traffic lane or travel lane marked with the high-occupancy vehicle lane symbol is a lane designated for vehicles of the specified type or category, or vehicles carrying no fewer than the specified number of occupants.

5. **Parking Space Dividing Lines** have the appearance of solid white lines indicating the boundaries of parking spaces. This means drivers must park within the marked parking space lines. Parking astride the lines or allowing any part of the vehicle to extend beyond the designated boundaries is prohibited.

6. **Mandatory Text on Road Surface** has the appearance of white text on the road surface, such as the words "Stop" (หยุด), "Reduce Speed" (ลดความเร็ว), "Drive Slowly" (ขับช้า ๆ), etc. This means drivers must comply with such text instructions.

192.body:
4. Edge line: Appears as a solid line, dashed line, or colored strip in white, except that the edge line on the side adjacent to a median island or directional traffic divider is yellow. This means it marks the outermost edge of the carriageway.

5. Lane line through intersection: Appears as a dashed or solid white line indicating the lane or traffic lane alignment in the intersection area. This means drivers should follow the indicated lane or traffic lane alignment.

6. Speed reduction line: Appears as multiple lines across the lane or traffic lane. This means drivers should slow down and exercise increased caution.

**Penalties for Violating Traffic Signals and Traffic Signs**

The Road Traffic Act B.E. 2522 stipulates that drivers must comply with signs and traffic signs as provided in Section 21, with a prescribed penalty of a fine not exceeding one thousand baht.

**Section 21** Drivers must correctly comply with traffic signals and traffic signs that have been installed or displayed on the road, or that traffic officers indicate. Traffic signals, traffic signs, and the meanings of traffic signals and traffic signs shall be determined by the Director-General and published in the Government Gazette, with illustrative examples included in the announcement.

**Section 152** Any person who violates or fails to comply with Section 21 shall be liable to a fine not exceeding one thousand baht.

193.body:
# Chapter 2: Safe Driving

On the roads in Thailand, a large number of people choose to use motorcycles because they are inexpensive, fuel-efficient, and require little parking space. However, since motorcycles do not have a structure to protect the rider, when an accident occurs, both the rider and passenger suffer serious injuries. Therefore, riders must always prepare themselves before every ride, as well as learn proper and safe motorcycle riding techniques.

## 2.1 Safe Driving Techniques

**1. Attire for Riding a Motorcycle**

When riding a motorcycle, the rider should wear appropriate clothing and use equipment that will help increase safety and reduce injuries from accidents, as follows:

1) Must wear a full-face safety helmet that meets the Thai Industrial Standards Institute (TIS/มอก.) standards, which has been tested and proven to reduce the danger from impact in the event of an accident.

2) The visor of the safety helmet must be clear enough to see road conditions clearly, even at nighttime.

3) Should wear long-sleeved shirts and long pants to reduce injuries from falling and sliding on the road surface.

4) Should wear full-finger gloves and closed-heel shoes to reduce potential harm to fingers and toes.

5) Caution: Do not allow any part of clothing to hang loose, as it may get caught in the wheels.

6) Proper wearing of a safety helmet: It should be the right size for the head. Adjust the chin strap to fit snugly around the head—not too loose or too tight—leaving just enough space to insert a finger for wearing comfort.

196.body:
3. Inspecting Motorcycle Readiness

A good rider must be knowledgeable about the "vehicle," regularly inspect and repair any defects, and understand and learn the operation of equipment as well as the various systems of the motorcycle, the details of which are as follows:

1. **"Fuel"** – Check that there is sufficient fuel.
2. **"Tires"** – Check tire pressure by squeezing; tires must not be flat or leaking, and tread depth must be greater than 1.6 millimeters.
3. **"Lights"** – Turn on all lights to verify they are functional by testing the headlight on both high beam and low beam, left and right turn signals on both front and rear, taillight, brake light, and indicator lights on the instrument panel.
4. **"Horn"** – Press to test the operation of the horn.
5. **"Engine Oil"** – With the engine off and the motorcycle parked on a level surface, check that the engine oil level is at an appropriate level—neither too high nor too low.
6. **"Chain"** – Check that the chain is lubricated by test-spinning the rear wheel. Check the tension; a chain that is too tight will cause the engine to work harder, and one that is too loose risks the chain coming off and causing an accident. Therefore, when pressing the chain, it should give 10–20 millimeters.
7. **"Throttle"** – Check that the throttle snaps back immediately upon release.
8. **"Brakes"** – Check the brake fluid level and test that the brakes function properly. Check that the hand brake lever and foot brake pedal spring back immediately upon release.
9. **"Clutch"** – Check that the clutch lever is not too loose; verify that the free play does not exceed 20 millimeters.
10. **"Side Mirrors"** – Inspect and adjust the viewing angle to eye level at all times, so that the ground level is visible at the center of the mirror and one's own shoulder is slightly visible.
11. **"Others"** – Check the driving license, copy of the vehicle registration book, license plate, and proof of tax payment, etc.

199.body:
8) Riding Posture

1. Eyes: Must look at the road ahead with a wide field of vision; do not stare at a single point.
2. Posture: Do not tense the shoulders, as this will reduce the efficiency of vehicle control.
3. Arms: Hold the handlebars in a relaxed manner—not too tight or too loose with elbows flared out.
4. Hands: Grip the handlebars lightly at the center of the grip, with wrists aligned with the arms, and place fingers on the brake and clutch levers.
5. Hips: Positioned at the rider's seat.
6. Knees: Facing toward the front of the motorcycle, gripping the fuel tank (if applicable).
7. Feet: Placed on the footrests with toes pointing forward, positioned at the gear pedal and brake pedal.
8. Do not sit with the body too upright.
9. Do not look too close to the front.
10. Do not spread or lift the legs outward, as this will cause instability.

5. Basic Controls

**Throttle:** Use the right hand to twist counterclockwise to increase speed, and twist clockwise to decrease speed.

**Hand Brake:** Use the right hand to squeeze the brake lever to apply the front brake, and release to cancel braking.

**Foot Brake:** Step on the brake pedal to apply the rear brake, and release to cancel braking.

**Clutch:** Use the left hand to squeeze the clutch lever to disengage power transmission from the engine before shifting gears, then gradually release the clutch to allow the engine to transmit power for riding.

200.section: 1) Starting and Shutting Off the Engine
200.body:
The rider should learn the basic engine controls of a motorcycle in order to understand the techniques for riding a motorcycle safely, as follows:

1) Starting and Shutting Off the Engine
1. Turn the key to the ON position.
2. Shift the gear to neutral (N).
3. In the case of an automatic transmission motorcycle, squeeze and hold the brake lever.
4. Press the engine start button or use the foot to kick the kick-starter to start the engine.
5. Slightly twist the throttle to maintain engine RPM and prevent the engine from stalling.

2) Shutting Off the Engine
1. Shift the gear to neutral (N).
2. Turn the key to the OFF position.

3) Using Turn Signal Lights
1. Push to the left to signal a left turn.
2. Push to the right to signal a right turn.
3. Press the center to turn off the turn signal light.

4) Controlling the Headlight and Using the Horn
1. Press the horn button to sound the horn.
2. Press the button up or down to select high beam or low beam.

5) Moving Off and Stopping
1. While the engine is running, squeeze the clutch (in the case of a motorcycle with a clutch), engage the gear, then gradually twist the throttle.
2. Gradually release the clutch (in the case of a motorcycle with a clutch) to prevent the engine from jerking and stalling.
3. Use the feet to support the motorcycle until it has moved a certain distance, then lift the feet up.
4. In the case of stopping, use both feet to support the motorcycle before it comes to a complete stop.
